## 分诊 · `domain:devx` / `priority:p2` / `pm:queue`

**Anchor read, not guessed.** The defect is *when the gate is selected*, so the fix lands in the CI derivation / always-run gate set ⇒ `domain:devx`. Confirmed on `origin/main` `f1d7872` (2026-09-05T00:30:54Z): `packages/client/src/envelope-caller-census.test.ts:246` — `const CENSUS = scanCallSites(REPO_ROOT);` at **module level** ⇒ whole-repo in what it reads, package-scoped in when it runs.

### Grade — p2

⭐ **The cost is measured, not modelled**, and the arithmetic is the whole card:

> **One PR-side red would have cost one author one re-push. Instead it cost five queue ejections and, four days later, a full diagnosis flight.**

#13596 added a gate refusal **string literal** containing two `client.analytics.query(` shapes. The census blanks comments but **deliberately leaves literals intact**, so it counted them: `expected 21 to be 19`. ⇒ It was a `scripts/**` change; **it could not have reddened on that PR**, and it reddened in the merge queue where speculative stacking ejected five PRs — **four of them measurably bystanders** inheriting the same `expected 21 to be 19` from a tree that already carried #13596's `+2`.

⭐ And the file's own header already says it out loud: *"invisible to every local gate a `scripts/**` edit derives."* ⇒ The property is known, written down, and unfixed.

Not p1: it fails **somewhere** — nothing merges broken. Not p3: five ejections and a four-day diagnosis is the most expensive single incident routed this round.

### ⛔ The axis fence — and it is the most important thing on this card

> **#13874 ruled the census's literal-versus-context distinction SUSPENDED** — that is the **WHAT-it-counts** axis, and it is settled. ⛔ **Do not reopen it.**
>
> This card is the **WHEN-it-runs** axis, and nothing has ruled on it.

Adopted and binding. ⭐ The two really are independent, and the card's formulation is exact: *a census that counts literals on purpose is fine; a census that can only report at the most expensive moment is a scheduling defect regardless of what it counts.* ⇒ ⛔ A PR that "fixes" this by teaching the census to skip literals has reopened a suspended ruling and not fixed this card.

### Boundary test

**A** (always-run set) and **B** (extension-based selection) both **widen** what runs on a PR; nothing checked is reduced, and no verdict changes. ⛔ No manual floor — but B *"a second, bespoke derivation rule beside the affected-package one"* is a new maintenance surface and should be a deliberate choice, not a convenience.

### ⚠️ The cost note that decides between A and B — do not skim it

> the scan cost is **import-time**, so a cheaper trigger **does not make the gate cheap — it makes it earlier.**

Measured: **~11.8 s wall, of which 92% is the import-time whole-repo scan** (import 10.85–11.85 s vs tests 174–210 ms). ⇒ **A costs ~12 s on every PR**, and B costs ~12 s on every PR that touches any code-extension file — which, for this repo, is nearly every PR. ⇒ ⭐ **A and B are much closer in cost than they look**, and B's extra maintenance surface may buy very little. ⛔ Do not choose B on the assumption that it is the cheap one without measuring how many PRs it would actually select.

⚠️ And the card names the real fork honestly: *"If ~12 s per PR is the blocker, the real question is whether the scan can be incremental, and **that is a different card**."* ⇒ ⛔ Do not widen this card into making the census incremental; ⭐ but if the answer to A/B is "neither, it's too slow", **that** is the card to file, and it should be filed rather than leaving this one to rot.

**C** (leave it, rely on #15397's better failure text — file, line, quote character, opening line of the offending literal) is a real option and its cost is stated correctly: *the next one still lands in the queue, just legibly.* ⚠️ Given the measured five-ejection incident, C is only defensible if the queue's ejection behaviour has changed since #13849.

⚠️ Carried forward as the card's own gaps: ⛔ the incident measurements are **#13849's, not re-run** by the filing seat (full evidence is on #13849), and ⛔ **not deduped**.

⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch — routing only.

Claim: PM seat `domain:devx @ objectstack` (#6023), session `session_012zGPuVVX3deAx9LdjK8jCk`, 2026-09-05T02:11Z — dispatching to an `os-dev` subagent on branch `claude/issue-15608-envelope-census-pr-side`. Ruling: the WHEN-it-runs axis only (⛔ #13874's WHAT-it-counts axis stays suspended — a fix that skips literals is refused). Prefer wiring the census into the PR-side run through the EXISTING whole-repo union mechanism in `ci.yml` (`check-cross-package-test-inputs --union-into`, the packages-whose-gates-read-the-whole-repo union) so a `scripts/**` change selects `@objectstack/client`'s suite; if that mechanism cannot express it, option A (always-run) with the ~12 s cost accepted and measured, ⛔ never a bespoke second derivation (B). ⛔ Not incremental scanning — if ~12 s is judged too much, file that card. Hot files: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` FREE; ⛔ `lint.yml` and root `package.json` are held by queued PRs — do not touch them. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched`, assignee set.
